key_insight: SSF-Net combines spatial and spectral processing to capture local interactions and global PDE coupling with near-linear complexity in spatial tokens.
engineering_relevance: The architecture offers a promising route to efficient PDE surrogates, though the abstract does not establish accuracy on specific solid-mechanics applications.
method: Multi-directional Mamba spatial branch reduces single-direction scanning bias.
Fourier spectral branch uses a block-diagonal MLP to capture global features efficiently.
A multiresolution convolutional encoder-decoder integrates spatial-spectral fusion blocks.
evidence_signal: Across a multi-task PDE benchmark with long-horizon stability assessment, SSF-Net reports lower prediction error and fewer parameters than attention- and convolution-based baselines.
watch_item: Near-linear asymptotic complexity does not establish practical speedups over FEM; solver comparisons and application-specific validation remain important.
paper_title: SSF-Net: A Spatial-Spectral Fusion Network for Accurate PDE Operator Learning
